top_story: Trump’s late-March threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure, followed on April 11 by warnings of renewed US strikes if the Islamabad talks failed, pushed Tehran to frame any pressure campaign as grounds for wider regional escalation. The April 12 talks ended without a deal, yet the Gulf ceasefire still held, leaving a tense pause in place rather than a settlement and preserving the risk that coercive signaling will spill back into open conflict. Across that same regional landscape, Israel’s killing of a nine-year-old Palestinian girl inside a Gaza classroom underscores that even where front lines are static, civilians remain directly exposed in spaces meant to provide safety. The immediate picture is a Middle East suspended between fragile interstate restraint and uninterrupted human devastation, with deterrent posturing failing to reduce the cost borne by ordinary people.
